title: Ha Long Bay
summary: Ha Long Bay is a seascape of limestone islands and towers in northeast Viet Nam, in Quang Ninh Province. UNESCO describes it as the most extensive example of marine-invaded tower karst globally. It was first recognized as a World Heritage site in 1994, and the Cat Ba Archipelago was added in 2023.

as_recorded.value: Ha Long Bay was first recognized as a World Heritage site in 1994 and 2000.

reviewer_note: The place has no single founding date, so the dates chosen are World Heritage recognition (1994) and the Cat Ba extension (2023). Sources differ on island counts (1,133 per UNESCO versus some 3,000 per Britannica) and on the size of the area. Britannica also mentions dragon legends and Hoabinhian culture, which are not used in the summary. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from UNESCO, Encyclopaedia Britannica; quotes machine-checked.)
